content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat milk (1% milkfat) is produced by removing most of the fat from whole milk. It retains the majority of the nutrients found in whole milk, including protein, calcium, vitamin D, and vitamin B12, but provides far fewer calories and saturated fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Low‑fat milk is a common choice in calorie‑controlled diets.
In many countries it is labeled as “1%” or “0.9%” milk.
Milk naturally contains lactose, a sugar that can cause intolerance in some individuals.
Low‑fat milk is quickly absorbed after intense workouts, delivering protein and electrolytes.
Pasteurization preserves most vitamins, but vitamin A is partially lost with the removed fat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A 250 ml serving provides about 8 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Delivers over 30 % of the daily recommended calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: With only 1 % fat, it helps control calorie intake and saturated fat consumption.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content makes it an excellent beverage for maintaining fluid balance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People lacking sufficient lactase may experience bloating, diarrhea, and discomfort after drinking milk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can cause skin reactions, respiratory symptoms, or anaphylaxis.

items.title: Vitamin A content
items.content: Because most fat is removed, vitamin A levels are lower than in whole milk; prolonged exclusive use may require an additional source.

items.title: Processing additives
items.content: Some brands add stabilizers or sweeteners; check the ingredient list if you prefer a clean product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Low‑fat milk works well with cereals, in smoothies, for sauces, baking, and as a base for protein shakes. It can be enjoyed cold or gently warmed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑taste.
